name: Glasgow Coma Scale

version.label: Adult GCS, structured approach
version.detail: Teasdale & Jennett 1974, with the 2014 structured assessment terminology (e.g. 'To pressure', 'Not testable'). Paediatric GCS is a different instrument and is not implemented here.

reviewStatus: Content drafted from primary sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
purpose: Standardised description of level of consciousness using eye, verbal and motor responses.
intendedPopulation: Adults and older children with impaired consciousness from any cause; most validated in traumatic brain injury.

inputs.label: Eye opening
inputs.help: Record the best response. Apply a stimulus only if there is no response to the previous level.

options.label: To sound
options.detail: Opens after spoken or shouted request.

options.label: To pressure
options.detail: Opens after fingertip, trapezius or supraorbital pressure.

options.label: None
options.detail: No eye opening; no interfering factor.

options.label: Not testable
options.detail: Closed by a local factor (e.g. swelling, dressing).

options.label: Oriented
options.detail: Correctly gives name, place and date.

options.label: None
options.detail: No audible response; no interfering factor.

options.label: Not testable
options.detail: A factor prevents communication (e.g. intubation, tracheostomy).

inputs.label: Best motor response
inputs.help: Record the best response from either upper limb.

options.label: Localising
options.detail: Hand brought above clavicle toward a head or neck stimulus.

options.label: Normal flexion
options.detail: Rapid flexion at the elbow, not predominantly abnormal.

options.label: Abnormal flexion
options.detail: Slow, stereotyped flexion of the arm at the elbow.

notTestable.label: Total not reported
notTestable.summary: A component is not testable, so a total score should not be reported. Communicate the components instead.
notTestable.detail: Substituting a value or summing the testable components misrepresents the patient.
notTestable.share: GCS {e_code} {v_code} {m_code} (total not reported: component not testable)

states.label: No impairment measured
states.summary: No impairment of consciousness measured by GCS at this assessment.
states.detail: A GCS of 15 does not exclude significant intracranial pathology, focal deficits or later deterioration.

states.label: Mild impairment range
states.summary: Within the mild range used in traumatic brain injury classification (GCS 13–15).
states.detail: Reassess serially. Subtle changes within this range can be clinically important.

states.label: Moderate impairment
states.summary: Moderate impairment of consciousness (TBI classification GCS 9–12).
states.detail: Assess the cause, trajectory and associated findings according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

states.label: Severe impairment
states.summary: Severe impairment of consciousness (TBI classification GCS 3–8).
states.detail: Assess airway, ventilation, oxygenation, neurological status and other reversible causes according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

insights.text: Motor score is the component most strongly associated with outcome. Abnormal flexion, extension or no motor response warrants close attention to the trajectory.
The total is low while the motor response is relatively preserved. Two patients with the same total can differ substantially; always report the components.
With the verbal component not testable (e.g. intubated), the FOUR score includes brainstem reflexes and respiration and does not depend on verbal response.
Report components with the total, e.g. E2 V3 M5 = 10. The components carry more information than the sum.

limitations: Developed for describing consciousness; its severity bands are derived from traumatic brain injury.
Verbal response cannot be assessed in intubated or aphasic patients.
Does not assess brainstem reflexes, pupils or lateralising signs.
Inter-rater variability is higher in the intermediate range and with inexperienced assessors.
confounders: Spinal cord injury or limb injury limiting motor response
commonErrors: Reporting a total when a component is not testable, or assigning 1 instead of NT.
Recording the worst rather than the best motor response.
Testing motor response in the lower limbs (spinal reflexes can mislead).
Applying painful stimulus before checking the response to sound.
Scoring 'localising' when the hand does not cross the clavicle.
doesNotTellYou: Whether a focal or brainstem lesion is present.
The need for any specific intervention.
Prognosis on its own, outside an appropriate model.

sources.citation: Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness. A practical scale. Lancet. 1974;2(7872):81-84.
Teasdale G, Maas A, Lecky F, et al. The Glasgow Coma Scale at 40 years: standing the test of time. Lancet Neurol. 2014;13(8):844-854.
Structured approach and terminology: glasgowcomascale.org (Institute of Neurological Sciences, Glasgow).

licensing.status: Implemented in original wording with attribution
licensing.note: The scale criteria are widely published. Official GCS teaching aids, charts and translations from glasgowcomascale.org are not reproduced.

guide.what: A three-component scale (eye, verbal, motor) that describes a patient's responsiveness. Totals range from 3 to 15.
guide.whenUseful: Initial and serial neurological assessment, handover communication, trauma triage, and as an input to other scores (WFNS, ICH Score, GCS-P).
guide.howToCalculate: Check for factors that interfere with each response. Observe first, then stimulate: sound before physical pressure. Record the best response for each component. Report components and, only when all are testable, the sum.
guide.clinicalContext: Trends matter more than a single value. A fall of 2 or more points, or of 1 point in the motor score, is commonly treated as significant deterioration in TBI practice; respond according to local protocol.
